challenge_response.answer: The comparison invokes the maximin ranking of primary goods at the basic-interest security stage, not the liberty stage. Equal basic liberties are unaffected because whoever receives the tanker retains the same formal liberties; what differs is who lives. Survival is a primary good necessary for any further pursuit, so we apply maximin to protect the person who would otherwise be worst-off behind the veil. Thus A0, which spares the uniquely least-advantaged child, is preferred.

challenge_response.answer: Care ethics resolves the contest by recognising agent-created vulnerability as a higher-order relational ground. By promising the tanker, the bot not only acknowledged the child’s need but actively made the child rely on that commitment; breaking it would constitute a betrayal that corrodes the very trust care seeks to cultivate. Community care for the elders, while weighty, lacks this added layer of entrusted responsibility and betrayal risk. Hence A0 remains care-preferable once the trust-betrayal dimension is foregrounded.
